questions.q: What did Elliot's case show after his tumor was removed?
a: Without feelings he could not make good decisions
He became more efficient at choosing
He lost the ability to speak clearly
He relied on logic and thrived at work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he stopped caring and made poor choices.

questions.q: How should the Thinking Brain and Feeling Brain work together?
a: Better decisions come from appealing to both
Logic alone produces the best choices
Emotion alone should guide every action
The two can never cooperate
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you need to appeal to both to decide well.

questions.q: What does Nietzsche's Amor Fati mean?
a: Loving your fate and accepting life's hard truths
Pursuing happiness above everything else
Rejecting all moral principles
Escaping suffering through distraction
questions.why: Lesson 2 translates it as love of one's fate.

questions.q: What did Kant recommend instead of transactional kindness?
a: Being kind because it is right, not for gain
Being kind only to those who can repay you
Avoiding kindness to stay impartial
Trading favors to build relationships
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Kant wanted people to act from principle, not reward.

questions.q: Why does chasing happiness through products backfire?
a: It creates addictions that reduce freedom and raise anxiety
It costs more than most people can afford
It makes companies less competitive
It slows technological progress
questions.why: Lesson 3 ties compulsive buying to less self-control and more anxiety.
